pr_title: executor: fix load-data result when field term be the prefix of line term
pr_body: Signed-off-by: lysu ### What problem does this PR solve? Issue Number: close #22578 Problem Summary: `load data` will miss line when field-term be the prefix of line-term like issue said ### What is changed and how it works? What's Changed, How it Works: for most usage, check field-term first is more efficient, so we only need check line-term first when field-term be the prefix of line-term - add test case for "field-term be the prefix of line-term" and "line-term be the prefix of field-term" - extract common cmp logic and reorder check order when"field-term be the prefix of line-term" ### Related changes - Need to cherry-pick to the release branch ### Check List Tests - Unit test - Manual test Side effects - n/a ### Release note - Fix wrong load-data result when field term be the prefix of line term --- This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/pingcap/tidb/22585)
pr_comments:

issue_context.title: `load data local infile` can only load one row when field-term be the prefix of line-term
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)

```
bash>  cat t.csv
1|
2|
3|
4|
5|

mysql> create table t(a int);

bash>  mysql -u root -P 8012 -h 172.16.5.85 -D tpch_1 --local-infile=1 -e "load data local infile '/data1/jaysonhuang/tiflash/integrated/t.csv' into table t fields terminated by '|' lines terminated by '|\n'"

mysql> select * from t
```

### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)
There are 5 rows in table `t`

### 3. What did you see instead (Required)
There is only 1 row in table `t`
```
mysql> select * from t;
+---+
| a |
+---+
| 1 |
+---+
```

### 4. What is your TiDB version? (Required)

<!-- Paste the output of SELECT tidb_version() -->
```
mysql> select tidb_version();
+-------------------------------------------------------------------+
| tidb_version()                                                    |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Release Version: v4.0.0-beta.2-2063-gc54932640                    |
| Edition: Community                                                |
| Git Commit Hash: c54932640bcdd4dd7aeeb9ca6f4f41106974beb5         |
| Git Branch: master                                                |
| UTC Build Time: 2021-01-27 10:11:59                               |
| GoVersion: go1.13                                                 |
| Race Enabled: false                                               |
| TiKV Min Version: v3.0.0-60965b006877ca7234adaced7890d7b029ed1306 |
| Check Table Before Drop: false                                    |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------+
```
comments:
I think this may not a bug.

I can load data successfully using `mysql -u root -P 4000 -h 127.0.0.1 -D test -e "LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE '~/Downloads/debug/t.csv' INTO TABLE t LINES TERMINATED BY '\n'"`
Looks that the behavior of MySQL 5.7 is the same with TiDB, could you check it again?

Here's what TiDB/MySQL received:

```
mysql> load data local infile '/home/bb7133/t.csv' into table t fields terminated by '|' lines terminated by '|\n';
Query OK, 1 row affected, 1 warning (0.01 sec)
Records: 1  Deleted: 0  Skipped: 0  Warnings: 1

mysql> show warnings;
+---------+------+----------------------------------------+
| Level   | Code | Message                                |
+---------+------+----------------------------------------+
| Warning | 1265 | Data truncated for column 'a' at row 1 |
+---------+------+----------------------------------------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec)
```

I check the data and find that it should be `'|\n'` for line terminated, and the t.csv is rows end with '|\n'(data generated by TPCH script). I have updated the Minimal reproduce step, PTAL again @bb7133 @XuHuaiyu

I have updated the input to be
```
bash>  cat t.csv
1|
2|
3|
4|
5|
```
Try to refresh your browser?
I got your point, thanks for reporting and it is introduced by #21895.

this only affect on 5.0 / master, 4.0's modification has be reverted

it also need special prefix term to trigger...maybe we can change severity to major first
